verdicts.title: Ehrhart Limits
verdicts.abstract_excerpt: We introduce the definition of an Ehrhart limit, that is, a formal power series with integer coefficients that is the limit in the ring of formal power series of a sequence of Ehrhart $h^*$-polynomials. We identify a variety of examples of sequences of polytopes that yield Ehrhart limits, with a focus on reflexive polytopes and simplices.
verdicts.judge_reasoning: The abstract discusses 'Ehrhart limits' as formal power series limits of h*-polynomials for sequences of polytopes (especially reflexive ones), which shares the Ehrhart-theory vocabulary but does not address minimal generators of Ehrhart semigroups, binary hypercubes, or communication complexity.

verdicts.title: Quantum communication complexity of linear regression
verdicts.abstract_excerpt: Quantum computers may achieve speedups over their classical counterparts for solving linear algebra problems.
